controls.title: Record-keeping — automatic logging for high-risk AI systems
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the AI system itself is conformant with Art. 6 risk classification, Art. 9 risk management, Art. 10 data governance, Art. 13 transparency, Art. 14 human oversight, or Art. 15 accuracy and robustness. The chain is the logging substrate; it does not substitute for the conformity assessment.
controls.what_we_prove: Events emitted by an in-scope high-risk AI system to the chain are stored with tamper-evident ordering, signed timestamps, and cryptographic anchoring. An auditor or notified body can reconstruct the exact sequence of events for the duration of the retention period (per Art. 19, ≥6 months unless otherwise specified).

controls_out_of_scope.reason: risk classification of AI systems is a legal/technical determination, not chain-evidenced
risk management system is a process-level obligation
data and data governance for training/validation/testing is an upstream data-quality concern
technical documentation is document-level, not chain-evidenced
transparency to deployers is a documentation/UX obligation
human oversight design is architectural, not chain-evidenced (specific human-oversight events may be logged but the oversight design is not)
accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity testing is a pre-deployment assessment
quality management system is an organizational process
log retention duration is the controller's obligation; we provide the durable substrate but do not enforce a minimum retention
conformity assessment procedures are external/notified-body activities
EU declaration of conformity is a document-level artifact
post-market monitoring system is a process obligation
